issues.legal_issue: A person who is not bound by the arbitration agreement invoked for a dispute cannot be made a party to the arbitration under that agreement.
material_facts: The borrower and developer entered into a construction agreement containing an arbitration clause; the lender was not a party to that agreement.
The borrower invoked that clause to arbitrate claims arising from the developer’s alleged failure to complete the apartment.
The borrower also had a separate loan agreement with the lender containing an arbitration clause, but the developer was not a party to the loan agreement and the borrower did not invoke that clause.
The alleged tripartite agreement did not contain an arbitration clause.
issues.conclusion: The lender could not be included in the arbitration based on the construction agreement. The appointment remained effective for disputes between the borrower and developer, and the court should exclude a non-party to the invoked arbitration agreement or make clear that the arbitration is limited to parties bound by it.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 7 and 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 require an arbitration agreement applicable to the dispute between the parties to be referred. The Court relied on Jagdish Chander v. Ramesh Chander, 2007 (5) SCC 719, Yogi Agarwal v. Inspiration Clothes & U, 2009 (1) SCC 372, and S.N. Prasad v. Monnet Finance Ltd., (2011) 1 SCC 320. An arbitration clause in a separate contract does not permit a party to be joined in an arbitration concerning another contract, and a non-party impleaded in a section 11 proceeding must be deleted or expressly excluded from the arbitration.

predicates.section_eleven_appointment_proceeding: A party sought appointment of an arbitrator through a court proceeding of this kind.
predicates.invoked_agreement_binds_claimant_and_dis: The claimant and the party against whom the underlying dispute was raised entered into the agreement containing the invoked arbitration clause.
predicates.proposed_arbitration_party_not_bound_by_: The additional party sought to be included in the arbitration did not enter into, or otherwise become bound by, the agreement containing the invoked arbitration clause.

issues.definition: When an arbitrator is sought through this kind of court proceeding under an agreement binding the claimant and the dispute counterparty, an additional party not bound by that agreement is excluded from the arbitration.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot be referred to arbitration on a claimed dispute where no claim or demand was asserted against that party and refused before the appointment proceeding.
material_facts: Before filing the appointment proceeding, the borrower demanded compensation from the developer and invoked arbitration against it.
The borrower did not previously give the lender notice of a claim, demand relief from it, or seek arbitration of a dispute with it.
The borrower did not invoke the arbitration clause in the loan agreement in the appointment proceeding; the claims against the lender were raised there for the first time.
issues.conclusion: No dispute existed between the borrower and lender for referral to arbitration when the appointment proceeding was filed, so the lender could not be included in the arbitration on those claims.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 7 and 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, a dispute for referral arises when one party to an arbitration agreement asserts a claim or demand against the other and the other refuses or denies it. An arbitration agreement and a dispute referable under that agreement are conditions precedent to appointment of an arbitrator.

predicates.section_eleven_appointment_proceeding: A party sought appointment of an arbitrator through a court proceeding of this kind.
predicates.no_pre_application_claim_and_refusal_aga: Before the appointment proceeding, the claimant had not asserted a claim or demand against the proposed arbitration party that the party then refused or denied.

issues.definition: If a party seeks an arbitrator through this kind of court proceeding but had not first asserted a claim against the proposed arbitration party that the party refused or denied, there is no existing dispute to refer against that party.
